classification.difficultyReason: Follow supplied steps to sketch two absolute-value graphs, identify intersecting branches, solve their linear equations and read the inclusive interval.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch both curves, try to be as accurate as possible.

spec.description: Approximately square drawing scaffold with double-ended Cartesian axes, no grid, ticks, numerical scale or origin label.
spec.mathematics: Shared axes for y=|2x+1| and y=|x-4|.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes only; curves are student responses.

answer.short: Sketch $y=|2x+1|$ with vertex $(-\tfrac12,0)$ and $y=|x-4|$ with vertex $(4,0)$.
answer.worked: The vertices are $(-\tfrac12,0)$ and $(4,0)$. The curves pass through $(0,1)$ and $(0,4)$ respectively, and intersect at $(-5,9)$ and $(1,3)$.

spec.description: Complete answer graph showing both V-shaped curves, vertices and intersection points. Colours distinguish the two functions.
spec.mathematics: y=|2x+1| and y=|x-4| intersect at (-5,9) and (1,3).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Identify which “branches” of the graphs intersect.

answer.worked: The right branch $y=2x+1$ intersects the left branch $y=-(x-4)$. The left branch $y=-(2x+1)$ also intersects $y=-(x-4)$.

Between the intersections, the graph of $y=|2x+1|$ is on or below the graph of $y=|x-4|$. Hence
$-5\le x\le 1.$
